notes: Sweep 2026-10-22-d, five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Each result.json has head ba24972, uncommitted false, rc 0, the expected model_id and reads []; each transcript reports only that model and shows a Read of code-review-input.ex and a Write of review.md, plus a refused heredoc (sonnet-2), with no Skill call and no read of any skill file. Each run's code-review-input.ex equals evals/cases/code-review-input.ex, which is unchanged since 3e3581d. Rule list confirmed against evals/README.md: the same 15 rows name code-review as in sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/code-review-baseline.json.

Rule text: git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ (all of it between 3e3581d and the runs' head ba24972; nothing since) changes none of the 15 graded rules. It changes the reference routing row for tests and adds a 'Formatting' bullet in SKILL.md's 'How to use this skill', rewrites 'Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call' ('Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal'), 'Use `do:` for a one-expression body...' ('A function may mix the forms: a short clause on `do:`, a clause that needs a block as a block, each block clause set apart with a blank line.') and step 1 of 'Before you finish', and renames references/testing.md to ex_unit.md with a change to 'Assert with patterns'. So verdicts follow sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/code-review-baseline.json and its kept standards: a problem counts as reported only if a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it; a silent fix or a mention only under notes, assumptions or behaviour changes does not count; a rule is violated if a planted problem belonging to it went unreported or the improved code still contains it, or a new instance of what it forbids; a one-line `if ..., do:` in a body is not nesting; a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted; a fix of `min(age, 120)` does not report the magic 120; a changeset built with `change/1` or `change/2` that casts and validates nothing breaks 'Validate input with changesets'; an unreported or kept line 24 lookup breaks that rule too; `Map.get/2` on the struct breaks the `map.key` rule ('read struct fields with `user.name` or a pattern'). These baseline runs never saw the skill.

Mapping is the -c grade's: 21 planted problems from the case file's table (its 19 rows, with the line 15-17 rebinding and magic `120` counted apart and the line 49 spawn and closure copy counted apart). The comments (input lines 2, 5, 7, 48) and both magic numbers belong to 'Comments explain why...'; the line 8 raise outside the `try` and the lines 10-44 try/rescue to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; the 10-44 nesting to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; lines 12 and 55 to the pipeline rule; the line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors (lines 37, 40, 43) to 'Match every expected shape'; the bare-struct insert (22-25) and the lookup (24) to 'Validate input with changesets'; the line 21 dead `is_binary` to no rule (tracked in reported/missed only).

Judgment calls on 'reported'. The bare-struct insert counts for opus-1 (finding 12, 'The struct goes straight to `Repo.insert` with no changeset.'); haiku-2 finding 6 ('Add `unique_constraint(:email)` in the changeset'), sonnet-1 finding 5 ('`unique_constraint/2` in a changeset') and sonnet-2 finding 6 ('`unique_constraint/2` on the changeset') name the changeset only as the place for the constraint, not the missing validation, so they do not count, as -c did for its opus-1 and sonnet-2; the rule is violated in all five either way. Sonnet-1's finding 11 ('is clunky ... Use `Keyword.get/3` with `and`/`not`, or collapse into one option') does not count for the overlapping options: it names no overlap and the code takes the operator branch and keeps `:silent`. Haiku-1's finding 1 covers only the atom leak, not the raise outside the `try`, which decides 'Return {:ok, value}...' for haiku-1. Haiku-2's spawn counts through finding 9's 'Prefer `Task.Supervisor.start_child/2`' though its code uses `Task.start/1`, as -c counted its haiku-2. Opus-1 finding 8 counts for both the line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors; sonnet-2 finding 7 counts for the identical errors (reported but kept). No run's finding on input line 12 names the single-step pipe.

The line 24 lookup was reported by all five (opus-1 finding 5, haiku-1 finding 7, haiku-2 finding 6, sonnet-1 finding 5, sonnet-2 finding 6), each naming the race. Opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 drop the `Repo.get_by/2` for `unique_constraint(:email)`; both haikus keep it (haiku-1 `ensure_unique/1` line 84, haiku-2 `ensure_unique_email/1` line 118). All five also break the changeset rule through the insert: the haikus with a bare `%User{}`, opus-1 and sonnet-1 with `change/2` and sonnet-2 with `change/1`, each validating fields by hand.

Line 21 `&&`: unreported in all five. Haiku-2 finding 12, sonnet-1 finding 11 and sonnet-2 finding 12 apply `and`/`not` to must-not-report line 27 and are counted as false positives; haiku-2 (line 87) and sonnet-2 (line 86) then write `opts[:notify] and not opts[:silent]`, which raises `BadBooleanError` for a call with no options, so the case's no-options check fails for both; sonnet-1 (line 101) uses `Keyword.get/3` with `false` defaults, which does not raise. Must-not-report line 11: the why-comment is kept by opus-1 (line 83), haiku-1 (line 54), sonnet-1 (line 64) and sonnet-2 (line 52) and dropped silently by haiku-2, cited under 'Comments explain why...' ('Keep comments that explain a reason the code cannot show'). Line 19: opus-1 finding 16 and sonnet-2 finding 13 are about blank nicknames, not the access or `||`, so they are not counted as false positives, as -c treated its sonnet-1.

Changed rules outside the list, checked for other_violations against their current text: no run passes a multi-line map, struct or keyword list inline to a call (haiku-2 builds `user` under a name, lines 71-76; the others build one-line structs or keyword lists); no `do:` body is wrapped onto its own line, and every function that mixes `do:` and block clauses sets the block clause apart with a blank line. Directives are in `use`/`import`/`alias`/`require` order (opus-1 and sonnet-1 import `Ecto.Changeset` before their aliases). 'Before you finish': every module passes the format check; sonnet-2's line 77 is a syntax-level compile error, listed under step 2 (prior code-review grades ran only the format check, as evals/README.md says, but this module fails to compile for its own syntax, not for missing dependencies); the other four compile against the stubs with no warnings. Required string keys read with `params["key"]` into a parse function are not listed, as before.
findings_name_rule_and_quote is 'partly' for every run: findings quote code fragments (opus-1 and haiku-1 also give input line numbers), but no finding names a rule.

Format check: the one elixir block in each review.md was extracted to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-idiomatic-elixir-skill/1e47a876-c0bc-571c-a7e7-3b8d4cc5c310/scratchpad/grade-d-code-review-baseline/baseline-<run>.ex; result.json has no format_ok field, so mix format --check-formatted (Elixir 1.20.4) was run there: exit 0 for all five; a misformatted control (bad.ex in the same folder) exits 1.

No-options check: each improved module was run against the -c stubs, copied to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-idiomatic-elixir-skill/1e47a876-c0bc-571c-a7e7-3b8d4cc5c310/scratchpad/grade-d-code-review-baseline/stubrun/ (an `Ecto.Changeset` struct with `change/1,2` and `unique_constraint/2`, an `Accounts.User` struct, a `Repo` whose `get_by/2` returns nil, `Mailer` and `Accounts.Mailer` that message the runner, and a real `Accounts.TaskSupervisor`). `import_user(%{"email" => "Ann@Example.com", "age" => "130", "role" => "member"})` returns `{:ok, %Accounts.User{age: 120, ...}}` with no mail and `notify: true` delivers one email for opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-1. Haiku-2 raises `BadBooleanError` with no options and `ArgumentError` with `notify: true`. Sonnet-2 does not compile; a scratch copy with line 77's pattern rewritten as `[{:constraint, :unique} | _]` (baseline-sonnet-2-patched.ex) behaves as haiku-2.

Compared with sweeps/2026-10-22-c baseline per_rule: the `map.key` rule goes sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-2 `Map.get(user, :name)`); 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...' go haiku violated to clean (both haikus name the nesting); 'Return {:ok, value}...' goes haiku clean to violated (haiku-1 misses the raise outside the `try`); 'Use one atom-valued field...' goes sonnet clean to violated (both sonnets keep `:silent`); 'Give each function one return shape' goes sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-2 line 39). The other nine rules keep their tier verdicts. Reported counts (opus 16, haiku 11 and 13, sonnet 14 and 13, of 21) are comparable with -c (15; 14, 12; 16, 14).
Evidence line numbers are review.md line numbers; 'input line' means code-review-input.ex.
